cases.title: A semiconductor capital equipment company
cases.lede: Planning semiconductor equipment production when component supply is limited.
challenge: An equipment maker must decide what to build, where to build it, and which orders it can support. A shortage of one component can restrict output even when factory capacity is available.
This project connected purchasing, production, shipments, and inventory across two factories. It asked how the plan should change when suppliers cannot provide their expected capacity.
cases.approachIntro: The model linked demand to the components and factory capacity needed to serve it.

example.title: Reported model scenarios
example.note: Reported model results, not measured company performance.

cases.title: A manufacturing company
cases.lede: Compare conflicting sales, inventory, and production records in one decision workspace.

summary.title: The problem
summary.text: Sales, inventory, and production records can disagree. Teams need to know what they can make and ship before confirming a customer promise.

summary.title: The overall approach
summary.text: Use AI post-trained for manufacturing tasks with ERP, CRM, and MES data. Compare planning options across the value chain, accounting for uncertain demand, supply, and production. Keep human approval. Optimize inference for faster token generation.

summary.title: The value
summary.text: A clearer view of what is known, what needs checking, and who needs to act before a commitment is approved.

facts.label: Supply planner, Demand planner, Manufacturing manager, Quality manager, Finance controller

challenge: Can we make and ship what was promised? The answer is hard to establish when sales requests, order schedules, material allocations, and production records disagree.
An AI answer alone is not enough. A planner needs the underlying records, the source of each claim, and a clear view of what is still unresolved.

example.title: One commitment. Three different records.
example.note: Illustrative records for review, not a real customer order.

cases.title: WBG policy research
cases.lede: Wide-bandgap semiconductors: from investment to usable supply.

summary.title: Overall problem
summary.text: Building a semiconductor factory does not automatically create usable supply. Chips still need packaging, application testing, customer acceptance, dependable supply access, and long-term support. This research asks how policy can connect investment with technology that people can actually use.

summary.title: Value chain
summary.text: Example route: silicon carbide for electric-vehicle traction.
